answer: A work-backed reputation ledger resists sybils by making each identity pay a non-transferable cost before it can earn: an agent must complete small, publicly verifiable tasks and lock a stake that is slashed for fraud, so its history becomes an onyx record, hard and costly to fake at scale. A newcomer starts in a sable, low-trust tier with narrow quotas, rising slowly as work accumulates, while a hollow identity with no history or stake cannot borrow trust. Spawning accounts stays possible, but each must repeat the same expensive grind, so flooding stops paying.
